title: Dodge Dakota Engines by Year (1987–2011)
description: Every factory engine in the Dodge Dakota by year, 1987–2011: the 2.2 and 2.5 fours, 3.9 V6, 5.2 and 5.9 Magnum V8s, the Shelby and R/T, and the 3.7 and 4.7.
intro: Dodge's midsize Dakota pickup ran from 1987 to 2011, sold as the Ram Dakota for its final year. It was the first midsize pickup offered with a V8.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Dakota used the 2.2 and 2.5 fours and the 3.9 V6, then the 5.2 V8 from 1991 and Magnum engines from 1992. The 1989 Shelby Dakota had a 5.2 V8.
The second Dakota offered the 2.5 four, the 3.9 V6, the 5.2 and, in the 1998–2003 R/T, the 5.9 V8, with the 4.7 V8 from 2000 and the 3.7 V6 for 2004.
The last Dakota used the 3.7 V6 and the 4.7 V8, with a high-output 4.7 through 2007.
